title: Parent-changed flag has no mechanism
evidence: layers.md:118-122 says each record whose parent changes MUST be flagged and the builder flags it; the reference example (layers.md:162) depends on it. No code in apps/ emits parent-changed; approval-reopened only compares a record's own fields.
fix: Implement parent-changed as a finding with a tier and a Checked by line, or demote the provision and record the gap as a known-gap.

title: Auto-approval: records or questions?
evidence: intent.md:50 says a tier-3 draft auto-approves after decideBy plus the veto window; model.md:176 allows approvedBy "auto (veto window)" on records. release.md:33: "No record auto-approves: the veto window decides tier 3 questions only."
fix: Pick one (recommended: only questions auto-approve). Fix intent.md:50, intent.md:66, model.md:176, and state where an auto-approved answer is recorded.

title: The standard cites its own draft decisions as settled
evidence: intent.md:124, 144, 194, 236 say "Settled by decision/0003 ... 0009". All nine docs/intent/decisions/*.md carry "status": "draft"; model.md:545-553 holds approval behind draft decisions.
fix: Approve decisions 0001-0009 before tagging, or say "Proposed by" until they are approved.

title: ballot is a MUST on the page, optional in the schema
evidence: intent.md:300: each draft question MUST name decider, decideBy and ballot. record.schema.json:934 questionEntry requires only question, decider, decideBy; recommended (needed for auto-approval) is optional too.
fix: Require ballot in questionEntry, and require recommended when tier is 3.

title: draft-without-decider does not check questions
evidence: intent.md:306 claims it reports on Intent questions. Checker.cs:229-243 tests the record's own decider and decideBy when status is draft, never questions[] entries.
fix: Extend the check to question entries, or reword the Checked by line to "draft records".

title: Aged questions never become known gaps
evidence: intent.md:66 and :302, model.md:768, release.md:279 say a draft past decideBy is reported as a known gap. Checker.Graph.cs:1181-1199 skips tier 1 and emits only question-aged (tier A) for tier 3; nothing creates a gap.
fix: Decide what a past-date tier-1 question does; make the pages describe question-aged, or implement the conversion.

title: Questions "carry risk", but the schema forbids it
evidence: intent.md:314: "Money and personal-data questions carry risk". questionEntry has additionalProperties: false and no risk field (record.schema.json:931-942).
fix: Delete the sentence and rely on the record's risk, or add risk to questionEntry.

title: The actor has three homes
evidence: model.md:95 docs/intent/actors/; templates/consumer/README.md:29 and system.md:182 behavior/actors/. intent.md:82 (Keep Intent in Its Homes) and the layout example at intent.md:346-373 list neither actors/ nor research/.
fix: Keep docs/intent/actors/ (actor is an Intent type), fix the template index and system.md, and add actors and research to intent.md.

title: The approval hash is defined four ways
evidence: intent.md:70 and model.md:340 say statements, results, output names, rules and steps. docs/guide/approval-hash.md:20 says every field except identity, workflow and approval data, then lists per-type fields (:26-57) that include features, basedOn, except, setBy, risk.
fix: State the rule once (the guide's per-type table) and link to it from intent.md and model.md.

title: requirement-unmeasured does not read the statement
evidence: intent.md:212-216: a requirement whose statement names a number MUST carry measure and dueBy; the check reports those. Checker.cs:1610-1620 selects requirements that already carry measure and asks for a check and a passing run.
fix: Reword the Checked by line to the real behavior, and add statement-number detection only if wanted.

title: Five quality-requirement fields are undocumented
evidence: The template (requirement-page.md:41-45) and schema (:1010-1014) carry target, conditions, check, runsOn, evidence; requirement-unmeasured depends on check. intent.md:222 names only stimulus, environment, response, measure, dueBy.
fix: Document the five fields on intent.md and say which are required.

title: Tier means three things, and tier 2 never appears
evidence: Risk tier 1 or 3 (model.md:344), a question's own tier field (record.schema.json:940), and check tiers G, S, A (model.md:370). model.md:378 mixes them in one sentence. No glossary entry for tier.
fix: Rename them (risk class, question priority, check tier), define each in the glossary, and say whether a question's tier must match its record's risk.

title: Requirement origin: one of three, or all?
evidence: intent.md:192 (Statement): name the origin in features, basedOn, or a deciding decision. intent.md:194 (Rationale): "Any requirement names in features ... in basedOn ... in setBy ... in risk".
fix: Rewrite the rationale: the origin is one of three; setBy and risk are separate fields.

title: Every draft glossary term fails the decider check, even with a decider
evidence: Found by running the Lantern example. RecordReader.cs:865-879 builds term records without Decider or DecideBy, while Checker.cs:225-243 reports draft-without-decider (tier G) when either is missing. Lantern's terms carry both fields and still produced 6 findings. The glossary template has neither field.
fix: Read decider and decideBy for terms in RecordReader.cs, add them to the glossary template, and add a test.

title: A journey alone clears requirement-unfulfilled
evidence: Checker.cs CheckFulfilment counts fulfills from rule, use-case and journey. In Lantern, three requirements passed the check with no Behavior record at all, because the journey names them in fulfills. Intent satisfies its own completeness check.
fix: Count only Behavior records as fulfilling, and keep the journey's fulfills as a connection for the book.

title: One feature's story is spread over three files with three groupings
evidence: Requirement pages group by topic, features by problem, journeys by goal (model.md:244-249), and a requirement's parent is its first feature, not the page it sits on. In the largest consumer 719 of 928 requirements name no origin and no journey aim matches a goal title (docs/intent/research/intent-hierarchy-evidence.md:30-32). Spec Kit, OpenSpec and Kiro each keep one unit holding narrative, requirements and acceptance together.
fix: Make the topic page the parent of its requirements by containment (the identifier already names it); turn features, basedOn and decides into connections with a coverage check scaled to risk.

title: decidedOn and approvedOn carry one date
evidence: intent.md:154 requires decidedOn on an approved decision; intent.md:162 requires approvedOn. The schema requires both (:1632, :1639). The decision template has decidedOn but no approvedBy, approvedOn or approvedHash.
fix: Use approvedOn only (or decidedOn only), and add the approval fields to the decision template.

title: Three lists of what the founder decides
evidence: layers.md:60: personal-data retention, person-observable freshness, tenant-, market- or date-varying defaults. intent.md:312: "retention period, observable freshness, tenant-varying figure"; intent.md:314 adds market and date. model.md:22 has a third wording.
fix: Keep the list in one place and link to it.

title: Founder is undefined, and competes with four names
evidence: founder appears about 40 times in docs/core with no glossary entry. The same role is called decider, approver, decision owner and owner; setBy: founder is an enum value.
fix: Define decider in the glossary; make founder one value of it, or replace founder in the core pages.

title: Intent never describes Behavior while Intent fields render Behavior
evidence: intent.md:13 says an Intent record never describes Behavior. intent.md:56 and model.md:390 put use-case goals, Then clauses and refusals in journey detail; intent.md:74 and :244 give two different never-lists.
fix: Keep one never-list in the Statement and label book lines that come from Behavior as context.

title: The authority ladder skips most Intent types
evidence: model.md:308: constraint > product > requirement > rule > use case > result > scenario. Goal, problem, feature, journey, actor, decision and research are not placed; intent.md:38-40 says decisions "explain" and also "set the position".
fix: State that the unplaced types carry no authority, or place each one; use one verb for decisions.

title: One-line rationale is a MUST that nothing enforces
evidence: intent.md:202 MUST; record.schema.json:983 does not require rationale, and no length rule exists. Only Reviewed for.
fix: Require rationale in the schema with a sentence limit, or demote to guidance.

title: The veto has no mechanism
evidence: glossary.md:1143: a recommendation auto-approves "unless vetoed". No field, command or status records a veto. scope.md:154 says MUST record review.vetoWindowDays; project-file.md:110 marks it optional.
fix: Define a veto (for example a question status) or drop "unless vetoed"; align required versus optional.

title: No defined way to answer a question
evidence: model.md:460: answering clears the gate. Questions have no status or answer field (record.schema.json:930-942) and no command names the answer step.
fix: Add a question status (open, answered, auto-approved) and say which command records the answer.

title: setBy has two value sets
evidence: Requirement setBy: founder | tenant (record.schema.json:1023). Setting setBy: founder | operator | tenant (:2710). model.md:424: a field holds one shape on every record.
fix: Use one value set, or name the setting field differently.

title: Tenant-set value versus tenant-varying default
evidence: layers.md:60: a tenant-varying default MUST be a draft question. intent.md:324-328 treats the receipt threshold as founder-approved default and tenant data at once, while a requirement carries one setBy.
fix: State the rule for a requirement whose default and value have different setters, or split it into two requirements.

title: Journey and actor body sections are not on the Intent page
evidence: ConsumerValidator.Pages.cs:30 requires Example and Between the Steps on journeys and :34 Summary on actors; intent.md names neither. Between the Steps restates each step's ifItGoesWrong.
fix: List the required sections on intent.md; drop Between the Steps or define it as branch order only.

title: Journey step fields: carried or optional?
evidence: intent.md:54: each step carries id, says, the actor walking it and ifItGoesWrong. record.schema.json:859-864 requires only id and says; the template says "or remove this line".
fix: Say which step fields are optional, or require them.

title: Several Intent provisions bundle many obligations
evidence: authoring.md:524-526 asks for atomic provisions. Record each choice as a decision (intent.md:152) bundles decides, options, three sections, changeWhen, basedOn and approval; also the feature, requirement-identity and requirement-page provisions.
fix: Split after the content fixes, one obligation per provision.

title: The question and veto rules live on many pages
evidence: The draft-question rule is restated in intent.md (3x), layers.md, model.md, agent.md, release.md; the veto window in about nine places. layers.md:134-142 repeats layers.md:102-112 for one case. The wording already drifts (see auto-approval).
fix: Keep one statement in model.md "Questions and Ballots" and link to it everywhere else.

title: The glossary lacks the Intent layer's own words
evidence: No glossary entry for Intent, Behavior, record layer, tier, decider, founder or approval. "Layer" means documentation depth (glossary.md:911-915).
fix: Add the entries; rename the documentation-depth term so "layer" means one thing.

title: Product decision is used and rejected
evidence: intent.md:377 and model.md:639 use "product decision"; glossary.md:269 lists "product decision" as a rejected term.
fix: Remove the rejection, or rename one kind of decision in both places.

title: A requirement page needs no owner or status
evidence: model.md:617: every page MUST name one owner and one status. requirementPage (record.schema.json:2589) requires only type and reviewBy.
fix: Require owner and status on the page, or state the exemption.

title: decision.basedOn accepts requirements on every decision
evidence: record.schema.json:330-340 lets any decision name requirements in basedOn. intent.md:154 says constraints and research; model.md:661 allows requirements only on technical decisions.
fix: Restrict requirement ids to technical decisions in the schema.

title: Business requirement means a goal everywhere else
evidence: kind: business is a dated value such as Lantern's EUR 2.50 fee. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and Wiegers use business requirements for the organization's objectives, which LiteSpec calls goals.
fix: Rename the kind to policy across the schema, intent.md, the template, the glossary and the book.

title: An applying constraint can stay unanswered, and its answer is written twice
evidence: The What It Requires section restates in prose what requirements citing the constraint in basedOn already say. No check reports a constraint with applies: true that no requirement cites; in the largest consumer 5 of 29 constraints are cited by nothing.
fix: Generate What It Requires from the requirements that cite the constraint, and add a check for an applying constraint nobody cites.

title: Three origin fields with a precedence rule, and goals excluded
evidence: A requirement's parent is its first features entry, else its first basedOn entry, else a deciding decision (model.md:235). A goal cannot be a reason at all, though goal-oriented methods such as KAOS refine goals into requirements.
fix: With the topic page as parent, one basedOn list naming any reason: goal, problem, feature, constraint, research or decision.

title: The page never says why each type exists or when to skip it
evidence: intent.md:17-32 gives one line per type. Newcomers see eleven similar records with no way to tell which to write first. This deck's "Questions Intent Answers" table and the write-when and skip-when notes are what is missing.
fix: Add a Concepts table to intent.md: question, record, write it when, skip it when, familiar name.

title: A law has no obvious constraint kind
evidence: The constraint kind enum is technical, organizational or convention (record.schema.json:1525), arc42's categories. The most common constraint, a law or regulation, fits none clearly; Lantern had to pick organizational.
fix: Add legal (or regulatory) to the enum, or state on intent.md which kind a law takes.

title: A journey states its goal twice
evidence: aim states the goal in words and serves names the goal record (intent.md:54). In the largest consumer no aim matches a goal title, so the two drift.
fix: Drop aim, or define it as a one-line summary of the walk.

title: A system journey is not a journey
evidence: intent.md:58-60 lets actor/recurring-job walk a journey, such as erasing data past retention. Story maps and use-case narratives walk a person toward their goal; scheduled work is a requirement a job fulfills.
fix: Keep person and staff journeys; state scheduled promises as requirements.

title: A LiteSpec research record names a consumer project
evidence: docs/intent/research/intent-hierarchy-evidence.md:11 names a consumer by name; AGENTS.md: "Never name a consumer project in it."
fix: Replace the name with "the largest consumer".

title: Decision number: four digits or any?
evidence: intent.md:381 says four-digit number; model.md:92 says <number>; record.schema.json:64 accepts [0-9]+.
fix: Enforce four digits, or say <number> on intent.md.

title: Actor kind: group or organization?
evidence: intent.md:30 "a person, group, or system"; schema enum person | organization | system.
fix: Say organization on intent.md.

title: Decision template names a type that does not exist
evidence: templates/consumer/decision.md:20 "constraint-applicability id".
fix: Use the record types the Links table lists for decides.

title: Templates claim to validate but carry placeholders
evidence: templates/README.md:27 says templates are valid against the schema; goal.md writes "tier": "<1|3>" where the schema wants an integer; research.md puts a path under url.
fix: Validate templates in CI with a placeholder marker, or use working values; move path sources to the path key.

title: Saying no lives in three places, one of them misnamed
evidence: product neverDoes (intent.md:92), a refused feature with refusedBecause (intent.md:124), and the requirement page's Refusals section (intent.md:184), where Refusal is also the Behavior term for a use-case ending (glossary.md:551).
fix: Product-wide limits in neverDoes, a declined offer as a refused feature; drop the Refusals section or rename it Out of Scope.

title: The "no outside rules" answer lives elsewhere
evidence: intent.md:134: a project with no outside rules records that answer too. The answer is constraints.answered in litespec.project.json, which the page never names.
fix: Name the project-file key on intent.md and link scope.md.

title: Containers use three suffixes, and area and topic name one idea
evidence: Intent has requirement-page; Behavior has setting-set, rule-set, entry-point-list and permission-list. A requirement page sits at docs/intent/<area>/<topic>.md while its identifier names only the topic (model.md:93, :131). Readers ask why only requirements get a page kind.
fix: One container suffix across the standard, one word for area and topic, and one sentence on intent.md saying why requirements are entries.

title: Transitions and data: the template writes a table, the checker reads a field
evidence: Checker.cs:1463 TransitionsOf reads the frontmatter transitions array (record.schema.json:1947). templates/consumer/aggregate.md has no transitions field and asks for a ## Transitions body table, which ConsumerValidator.Pages.cs:31 requires. The same holds for data and the Data table.
fix: Keep transitions and data in frontmatter only and let the book render the tables, or have the builder read the tables; never both.

title: requirement-unfulfilled ignores four fulfilling types
evidence: Checker.cs:1060-1061 counts fulfills only from rule, use-case and journey. model.md:198 and behavior.md:205, 223, 239, 253 let reactions, jobs, notifications and settings fulfill. A requirement kept only by a notification fails at tier G.
fix: Add reaction, job, notification and setting to CheckFulfilment, with a test.

title: Integration-event audience is rejected by the checker
evidence: behavior.md:107, record.schema.json:2421 and the template make audience a permission. RecordTypes.cs:90 allows audience to target only actor, and Checker.cs:574-576 raises invalid-field otherwise.
fix: Key the link-target table by record type, or rename the field (for example readers).

title: aggregate.kind is a MUST, yet optional everywhere
evidence: behavior.md:371 MUST declare its kind; :377 says consumer fails without it. Schema does not require kind and defaults it (:1918, :1934); the template says remove the line for an entity; Checker.cs:409-415 treats absent as entity.
fix: Require kind in the schema, drop the default, and write kind: entity in the template; or demote the provision.

title: Notification suppression lives in two places
evidence: behavior.md:229 and :1113: each sends edge carries its own if. effectEntry has no if and additionalProperties: false (record.schema.json:485-524). The notification carries suppressedWhen (:2304) instead.
fix: Keep one place: add if to effect entries, or delete it from the prose and keep suppressedWhen.

title: The retention schedule is unchecked and duplicated
evidence: The template writes records without a type; the schema requires rows (:2772). CheckRetention (Checker.Graph.cs:680-702) reads aggregate dataClasses, never the schedule. basis, period and enforcedBy are written on both.
fix: Generate the schedule rows from dataClasses, or check that each class appears with matching values.

title: cross makes its use case tier 1 is not true
evidence: access.md:35 says tenant cross makes the use case tier 1. ReviewQueue.cs:254-257 sets tier from risk only; cross routes to the security queue (Differ.cs:1626).
fix: Say "routes to the security queue", or derive risk: access from tenant: cross.

title: Three "consumer fails" claims the schema does not back
evidence: Job: behavior.md:1077-1083 lists seven fields; schema requires only kind (:2192). Command audit: :827-831; audit not required (:2041). Idempotency: :817-821; not required, and CheckIdempotency returns early when absent (Checker.cs:1968-1972).
fix: Add conditional required fields to the schema and checker, or correct each Checked by line.

title: onFailure has two shapes
evidence: Effects use a string pattern "retry (n, backoff) then dead-letter" (record.schema.json:481-484; use-case template:63). Reactions and jobs use { retry, deadLetter, surfacesIn, runbook } (:588-604; behavior.md:207). The effect string is never checked.
fix: One structured onFailure for every edge; remove the string form.

title: Derived refusals have no place in the precedence order
evidence: behavior.md:175: refusals stand in precedence order, first match wins. Derived .forbidden and .invalid-input are never written (:183), so their position relative to written refusals is unstated.
fix: State the order (for example forbidden, invalid-input, then written refusals) and check it.

title: Glossary status ignores the record layer
evidence: glossary.schema.json:106-109 allows draft | approved | retired for every term. model.md:446-452: Behavior records use reviewed. A behavior term can never be reviewed.
fix: Make the term status conditional on layer.

title: record-orphaned covers five types, the page names one
evidence: behavior.md:699-703 and model.md:511-513: a use case with neither serves nor fulfills. Checker.Graph.cs:209-221 applies it to use case, reaction, job, notification and setting, so a plain setting with no requirement blocks.
fix: Document the five types and the setting exception, or narrow the check.

title: step-unserved counts reactions but not jobs
evidence: behavior.md:1285 and model.md:519-523 say use case. Checker.Graph.cs:236-241 counts use cases and reactions; the schema lets jobs serve steps (:2226).
fix: State "use case, reaction or job" and count jobs.

title: The Links table misses ten written links
evidence: model.md:184 claims the table names every written link. Missing: computedBy, releasedBy, acceptedBy, enforcedBy, driver, consistency.because, wideningBecause, retention intent, processors.system, claims.requirement. RecordTypes.cs:83-127 misses several too.
fix: Add each to the Links table with its reads-as phrases, and to RecordTypes.cs.

title: 29 of 30 Reviewed for lines are not questions
evidence: authoring.md:192: Reviewed for asks the one question a reviewer answers and where to look. behavior.md:343, 365, 419 ... are statements; only :1185 is a question. layers.md follows the rule.
fix: Rewrite each as "Which X ...? Look at Y."

title: Concepts states obligations that Standards restate
evidence: authoring.md:101: obligations belong in Standards. behavior.md:34, 71, 88, 111, 123, 197, 229, 272 each state a rule in Concepts in different words from its Standard.
fix: Move each obligation to its Standard or delete the Concepts sentence.

title: Access and result standards appear on two or three pages
evidence: Derive generic refusals: access.md:221, behavior.md:933, model.md:740. Entry-point kind: access.md:291 and behavior.md:1233 with different checks. Give use cases results: model.md:691 and behavior.md:875. Connect use case to Intent: model.md:505 and behavior.md:693.
fix: Keep each provision on its home page and cite it from the others.

title: More schema gaps behind "consumer fails" claims
evidence: Notification lists eight fields, schema requires three (:2267). External-system operations list six, schema requires two (:793). Entry-point auth, integration-event trust, input source and classification are optional in the schema.
fix: Require what the provisions name, or rewrite the claims.

title: prose-missing is advisory but the provision is a MUST
evidence: behavior.md:993 MUST carry Goal and What Happens; Finding.cs:106 tier A. Consumer requires only Goal.
fix: Make it a convention, or make the check block.

title: The "either" verb kind is not in the Standard
evidence: behavior.md:147 lists answer, draft, summarize, translate as either; the Standard at :661-667 knows only query and command verbs. UseCaseVerbs.cs has VerbKind.Either.
fix: Add either to the Standard.

title: A permission-only verb exists in code only
evidence: UseCaseVerbs.cs:94-98 defines manage; access.md:151 uses permission/manage-copies; the page lists 43 verbs and says none is redefined.
fix: Document manage as a permission word, or remove it.

title: Passive link names break the naming grammar
evidence: model.md:426: a link is a present-tense verb; exceptions name readBy only. computedBy, releasedBy and reachedThrough are passive.
fix: List them as exceptions with a reason, or rename them across schema, templates, book and checks.

title: source, calls and owner each mean two or three things
evidence: source: transcribed provenance, CloudEvents source, input provenance. calls: an effect verb and the computed screen link. owner: a person from the owner list and the system owning a store.
fix: Rename the minority meanings (eventSource, invokes, storeOwner).

title: Four vocabularies for reach
evidence: Idempotency scope tenant | account | login | global; access tenant own | cross | public | none; data-class reach own-tenant | subject-wide | platform-wide; role scope platform | tenant | self; job scope is free text meaning what a run selects.
fix: One closed reach vocabulary, and a different word for what a job run selects.

title: Undefined words and undocumented fields
evidence: floorplan, "the notification module", the claim input source, effect before and forEach, onExhausted, external-system sends, receives and failure, runsWhere: external:<timer>, and "theme" appear in schema or templates without a definition on the page.
fix: Add a row or sentence for each, or remove the field.

title: Runbook is a Behavior record with no section
evidence: model.md:57 lists runbook; the consumer requires six sections for it; behavior.md has no concept or Standard, though jobs and reactions name runbooks.
fix: Add a Concepts entry and a Standard, or link the page that owns runbooks.

title: Platform-wide settings have no module
evidence: model.md:107 puts them at docs/behavior/settings/<name>.md, but the identifier is setting/<module>.<name> and the parent is the module.
fix: Allow a platform module, or make the product the parent with its own identifier form.

title: advisory freshness cannot name its authority
evidence: behavior.md:127: advisory names the authority deciding later. record.schema.json:400 pattern allows only bare advisory.
fix: Allow advisory (<authority>).

title: Erasure exemption reason and period are unchecked
evidence: behavior.md:447-451 MUST carry reason and future reviewBy; Checker.Graph.cs:791-798 checks reviewBy only. period is free text though behavior.md:51 says ISO duration; the schema already has isoDuration.
fix: Add the conditional requirements and use isoDuration.

title: A store carries no states is unchecked
evidence: behavior.md:393-399. The schema allows states on a store; the checker checks states only for non-store.
fix: Forbid states on store in schema and checker.

title: A live use case must name an entry point, silently
evidence: Checker.cs:427-431 requires reachedThrough for a live use case; the Standard at behavior.md:717-725 names only reference-unresolved, and does not say how a use case only a job issues is reached.
fix: State the minimum and the internal-use-case case.

title: Consumer checks have no tier
evidence: model.md:370: every check has a tier. About 30 Checked by lines name litespec consumer with no tier.
fix: Give consumer findings a tier, or state that schema validation always blocks.

title: Template defects that fail validation when copied
evidence: screen.md keeps both address and host; ids carry "(the use case's own name)"; refusal code shown as <module>.<reason> versus the Standard's <module>.<noun>-<state>; model.md:141 example reaction/spending.remind-approver fails the -on- rule.
fix: Fix placeholders and examples; keep instructions outside the JSON.

title: Audit wording contradicts itself
evidence: behavior.md:121 and :829: commands are audited by default with reason none. none means not audited.
fix: Say: reason none is not audited; set required to audit.

title: The page is 1387 lines with 94 provisions
evidence: Concepts runs about 325 lines and repeats Standards. Many Standards bundle field lists (job: seven fields, notification: eight).
fix: Split by folder home (domain model; use case; automation; edges; privacy), and let one provision point at the schema field list.

title: Example section: required Default, optional template
evidence: behavior.md:1357-1367 Default says every module, aggregate and use case carries an Example; the templates say "Optional. Remove this section".
fix: Align the convention and the templates.

title: Reaction effects need no timing, yet the Standard says every effect
evidence: behavior.md:775-781 each effect MUST carry its timing; reactionEffectEntry has no timing and behavior.md:203 lets reactions omit it.
fix: Scope the Standard to use cases and jobs.

title: Event tense has a check but no Standard
evidence: event-tense-mismatch (Finding.cs:110, tier A) exists; behavior.md:88 says past tense only in Concepts.
fix: Add a Standard citing the check.

title: The rule-name negation word lists differ
evidence: behavior.md:503 lists ten words; Checker.cs:62-63 also accepts nothing, refuses, refusal, blocked, rejected, non.
fix: Make the page and the code list the same words.

title: Words the page leans on without defining
evidence: independently testable goal (:111), "debated rows" (:407, :565), "internal words" (:615-619) whose list lives in Checker.Wording.cs.
fix: Define each or cite the list.

title: The glossary has no implementation layer
evidence: glossary.schema.json:49-53 allows intent | behavior only; behavior.md:1343 sends child entities and value objects to the glossary, and system.md:255 lists technical terms.
fix: Add implementation, or say which layer design words take.

title: Records never point down, yet Intent points down
evidence: model.md:225: records never point down. decides on a decision may name rules, permissions, roles, entry points and settings (model.md:188); actor (Intent) holds roles (Behavior) (model.md:215). intent.md:13: an Intent record never describes Behavior.
fix: Name decides (and holds, or move it onto the role) as the only permitted downward links, and reword model.md:225 and intent.md:13.

title: Nothing is computed from code versus backfill and transcription
evidence: principles.md:83 MUST NOT compute a record above Implementation from code; model.md:11 and intent.md:42 say the same. tools/model.md:36 backfill drafts Behavior from code; model.md:350-353 defines transcription.
fix: Name transcription as the one exception in all three places: draft-only, ended by adoption.transcriptionEndsWith.

title: The parent-changed flag that links the layers does not exist
evidence: layers.md:28, :118-122 and the reference example at :162 rely on the builder flagging children of a changed parent. No code emits it; approval-reopened compares a record's own fields only (Checker.Graph.cs:915-929).

title: Two documentation layouts
